conbody.p: With any new query requests, the Impala coordinator sends metadata requests to Catalog service and sends metadata updates to Catalog which in turn propagates metadata updates to hive metastore. With a pair of primary/standby Catalog instances, the standby Catalog instance will be promoted as the primary instance to continue Catalog service for Impala cluster when the primary instance goes down. The active Catalogd acts as the source of metadata and provides Catalog service for the Impala cluster. This high availability mode of Catalog service reduces the outage duration of the Impala cluster when the primary Catalog instance fails. To support Catalog HA, you can now add two Catalogd instances in an Active-Passive high availability pair to an Impala cluster.

To enable Catalog high availability in an Impala cluster, follow these steps:
Set the starting flag enable_catalogd_ha to true for both catalogd instances and the StateStore.

The active StateStore will assign roles to the CatalogD instances, designating one as the active CatalogD and the other as the standby CatalogD. The active CatalogD acts as the source of metadata and provides Catalog services for the Impala cluster.

To disable Catalog high availability in an Impala cluster, follow these steps:
Remove one CatalogD instance from the Impala cluster.
Restart the remaining CatalogD instance without the starting flag enable_catalogd_ha.
Restart the StateStore without the starting flag enable_catalogd_ha.

concept.title: Monitoring Catalog HA Status in the StateStore Web Page

conbody.p: A new web page /catalog_ha_info has been added to the StateStore debug web server. This page displays the Catalog HA status, including:
To access this information, navigate to the /catalog_ha_info page on the StateStore debug web server.

The StateStore instance continuously sends heartbeat to its registered clients, including the primary and standby Catalog instances, to track Impala daemons in the cluster to determine if the daemon is healthy. If the StateStore finds the primary Catalog instance is not healthy but the standby Catalog instance is healthy, StateStore promotes the standby Catalog instance as primary instance and notify all coordinators for this change. Coordinators will switch over to the new primary Catalog instance.

When the system detects that the active CatalogD is unhealthy, it initiates a failover to the standby CatalogD. During this brief transition, some nodes might not immediately recognize the new active CatalogD, causing currently running queries to fail due to lack of access to metadata. These failed queries need to be rerun after the failover is complete and the new active CatalogD is operational.

concept.title: Checking the Status and Readiness of CatalogD

conbody.p: The /healthz page of catalogd returns OK on both the active and the standby catalogd as soon as the service has started. The page does not show which instance is active, and it does not show whether the metadata is loaded. To find the active catalogd, check the catalog-server.active-status metric on the /metrics page of catalogd, which is true only on the active instance, or the /catalog_ha_info page of the StateStore.

Starting in , catalogd can report OK and an active status before it finishes loading the metadata. To check that the catalog is populated, see Catalogd Startup and Readiness in Metadata On-demand Mode.

By default, when the standby catalogd becomes the active instance, it resets all its metadata, as if you ran INVALIDATE METADATA, and loads the metadata again. You can configure the standby catalogd to keep its metadata cache instead. In this case, the new active instance applies the pending Hive Metastore (HMS) events before it becomes active, so that it does not use stale metadata. Set the following flags on both catalogd instances, because either of them can become the active instance:

ul.li: --catalogd_ha_reset_metadata_on_failover: The default is true, which resets all the metadata at failover. If you set it to false, the new active catalogd keeps its current metadata and applies all the HMS events that were generated before the failover. This flag is visible in the /varz page starting in .

--catalogd_ha_failover_catchup_timeout_s: The time in seconds that the new active catalogd waits for the pending HMS events to be applied. The default is 300. The flag is added in , and it is used only if --catalogd_ha_reset_metadata_on_failover is false.

--catalogd_ha_reset_metadata_on_failover_catchup_timeout: What the new active catalogd does if the pending HMS events are not applied within the timeout. The default is true, which resets all the metadata. If you set it to false, the catalogd becomes active with its current metadata, which might be stale. The flag is added in , and it is used only if --catalogd_ha_reset_metadata_on_failover is false.

conbody.p: The wait for the HMS events happens only at a failover. Regardless of the flags above, the new active catalogd resets all the metadata if the event processor is in an error state, or if it cannot get the latest event id from HMS in time.
The standby catalogd keeps its metadata up to date from the HMS events. Therefore, setting --catalogd_ha_reset_metadata_on_failover=false requires that all of the following are true:

ul.li: --hms_event_polling_interval_s is greater than 0. The default is 0.5.
--enable_insert_events is true. This is the default.

--enable_reload_events is true. The default is false, so you must set it explicitly. With this flag, catalogd fires an HMS event for the REFRESH and INVALIDATE METADATA statements, so that the other catalogd can process them.

conbody.p: To fail over with a warm metadata cache, also configure the tables to warm up, as described in Warming Up the Metadata of Critical Tables. The standby catalogd then loads the metadata of the listed tables, and the new active instance does not need to reload them.
